sections.presenting_complaint: Flare of atopic eczema for 2 weeks.
sections.history: Flare for 2 weeks (father initially said a month, then corrected), worst in the flexures, particularly the right elbow. Nocturnal itch disturbing sleep. No weeping, crusting, blisters or punched-out lesions. Systemically well. Recently started bubble baths. Using Epaderm once daily and hydrocortisone 1%. No personal history of asthma or wheeze. Father has hay fever; sister has asthma. Pet cat at home.
sections.medications_allergies: Epaderm emollient. Hydrocortisone 1% cream (over the counter). No known drug allergies.
sections.examination: Dry, erythematous, excoriated patches in both antecubital and both popliteal fossae, most severe in the left antecubital fossa. No weeping, crusting or vesicles. Mild cervical lymphadenopathy.
sections.impression: Moderate flare of atopic eczema; no signs of infection. Possible trigger: bubble baths.
sections.plan: Clobetasol propionate 0.05% once daily to inflamed areas on the body for 7 days, then hydrocortisone 1% if needed. Fingertip units explained. Epaderm 3–4 times daily and as a soap substitute (at least 500 g every 2 weeks). Stop bubble baths. Review in 2 weeks.
sections.safety_netting: Seek same-day review if painful sores, blisters or punched-out lesions, especially with fever or feeling unwell (possible eczema herpeticum).
